milk-data.note: Super Milk Fat-free has more carbohydrate (5.0 g versus 4.7 g), not less as the scheme says. Vitamin B12 values are equal.

coeliac.note: Coeliac disease is an immune disorder triggered by gluten, not simply an inability to digest it.

bottling.note: Water-bath processing is not suitable for all vegetables: low-acid foods require a validated pressure-canning process. The source’s short examples are examination guidance, not complete preservation recipes.

lipid-membranes.note: Lipids form cell membranes; human cells do not have cell walls. Retain the historical scheme wording with this correction.

reheating.note: FSAI advises reheating to at least 70°C throughout. For stews/casseroles the liquid should boil for 3–5 minutes to heat the meat through; the source’s 100°C example is not a universal core-temperature rule.

sectionAReview.selectionDecisions: All three true/false grids, the whole word bank, all required table headings, and open example counts remain one task each. Q2/Q11 have independent separately priced prompts. Q5 retains the unassigned 2+2+1+1 tariff without inventing which method gets two marks.

tooth-decay.note: Decay is driven by acids produced by oral bacteria acting on sugars/starches, not simply calcium deficiency.

popcorn.note: Water inside the heated kernel produces pressure; popping is not caused by starch absorbing fat.

cellulose.note: Cellulose remains non-digestible dietary fibre; cooking can soften the food without making cellulose digestible by human enzymes.

consent.note: Sexual activity requires freely given, ongoing consent; marriage does not confer entitlement to sex.

marriage-consent.note: Distinguish consensual arranged marriages from forced marriages. Do not generalise the scheme’s community example to all members of that community.

sectionBReview.selectionDecisions: Milk choice has two answer routes in one card; all meal courses/beverages are required; preservation and appliance are single open profiles. Required calcium, buying/storage, separation/divorce headings preserve exact tariffs. Cultural variations are open examples.

electrical-protection.note: An ordinary MCB provides overcurrent protection; an RCBO combines overcurrent and residual-current protection. MCBs do not universally contain RCDs.

poverty.note: CSO’s at-risk-of-poverty threshold is 60% of median equivalised disposable income, not the scheme’s 50% of average household income. Preserve the general relative-poverty definition and distinguish the erroneous threshold.
